name: Booking Microservices
description: A distributed booking platform organized around flight, passenger, booking, and identity services. It combines inter-service communication, asynchronous messaging, database persistence, security, and observability.
highlights: Services organized by business domain: API Gateway, Flight, Passenger, Booking and a Keycloak identity service.
Synchronous service-to-service calls over gRPC and asynchronous events through RabbitMQ.
Authentication and authorization with Spring Security, Keycloak, OAuth2 and OpenID Connect.
Observability with OpenTelemetry traces, Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards and Jaeger.
Architecture patterns explored: Domain-Driven Design, CQRS and Vertical Slice.
note: Built to explore microservices architecture and distributed backend design rather than a simple CRUD application.

name: GreenFlow
description: An intelligent irrigation-monitoring interface with sensor dashboards, historical visualizations, alerts, and automatic or manual irrigation controls. Gemini generates contextual natural-language recommendations from sensor data, with error handling and a rule-based fallback.
highlights: Real-time sensor dashboard with history and visualization.
Alerts, plus automatic and manual irrigation control screens.
Gemini 2.5 Flash through the @google/genai SDK: prompts built from sensor data produce natural-language recommendations.
Handles API errors and empty responses, with a local rule-based fallback.
note: The interface was built with AI-assisted coding.

name: Traffic Intelligence (TraffiQ)
description: A traffic-analysis platform combining vehicle detection and tracking with analytics for speed, incidents, and traffic patterns.
highlights: Vehicle detection and tracking with YOLOv8 and ByteTrack across user-defined lanes.
Per-lane analytics, speed analysis and incident detection.
Flask backend with an authenticated analytics dashboard and logging.
Prediction-related features based on traffic data.

name: Phone Retail POS
description: A full-stack POS and inventory management system designed for retail environments handling both serialized used devices and bulk accessories.
highlights: Stack taken from the repository README: Django REST Framework and PostgreSQL on the backend, React, TypeScript and Vite on the frontend, Docker Compose for infrastructure.
Domains listed in the README: catalog, inventory, sales, payments, customers, reservations, warranty, returns, exchanges, audit and reporting.
note: The repository is marked as under development.

name: CrowdSense
description: An intelligent stadium-navigation prototype designed to help spectators find shorter, less congested routes. Mohamed’s contribution was training the prediction model for path and crowd-traffic prediction.
highlights: Built by a team of three, which won first place at the RNsport Hackathon 2026.
Team concept: navigation arrows on the phone to guide spectators to their seat, toilets and food points.
Mohamed’s contribution: training the prediction model for paths and human traffic (Random Forest and Extra Trees) used to suggest the shortest or least crowded route.
note: Hackathon prototype — not deployed and without a public repository.
